title: Odysseus and the Sirens
text:
Before Odysseus left her island, the goddess Circe warned him about the Sirens. They sat in a meadow by the sea, surrounded by the bones of men, and sang so beautifully that any sailor who heard them steered toward them and never came home.

Odysseus made a plan. As the ship approached, he softened beeswax and pressed it into the ears of each of his men, so they could hear nothing. Then he had them tie him upright to the mast, hand and foot, so that he alone would hear the song. He gave them strict orders: if he begged or commanded to be set free, they must tie him tighter.

The wind dropped and the crew rowed toward the island. The Sirens saw the ship and began to sing. They called to Odysseus by name and promised him knowledge of everything that had happened at Troy and everything that happens on the earth.

Odysseus longed to go to them. He frowned and nodded at his men to untie him. Instead, two of them, Perimedes and Eurylochus, rose and bound him with more ropes, and the others rowed harder. Only when the song had faded behind them did the men take the wax out of their ears and untie their captain.
lesson: If you know a temptation will overpower your judgment in the moment, decide in advance and make it hard for your future self to give in.
people: Odysseus, his crew, the Sirens, Circe
